headline: TECK 72-HOUR STRIKE NOTICE at Highland Valley Copper — 944 workers could walk Oct 24 in BC's biggest open-pit
snippet: United Steelworkers Local 7619 issued a 72-hour strike notice to Teck Resources on October 21, giving the 944-member bargaining unit the legal right to walk off the job as early as 8:00 a.m. PT on October 24. Negotiations ended without agreement after Teck's revised monetary offer fell short of members' expectations following a 100% strike mandate vote; a stoppage at Highland Valley — one of Canada's largest copper mines producing roughly 140,000 tonnes annually — would meaningfully tighten already-stressed North American copper supply.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER HITS 110m at 1.86% CuEq at Kwanika BC — true-width 84m result extends Western Zone depth
snippet: NorthWest Copper Corp. (TSXV: NWST) reported drill hole K-26-346 at the Kwanika project in British Columbia's Omineca region returned 110.0 metres grading 1.86% copper equivalent (0.64% Cu, 1.10 g/t Au) — estimated true width of 84.3 metres — from 378 metres depth in the Western Zone. The intercept continues a run of wide copper-gold results at a project where a preliminary economic assessment outlined a 15,000 tonne-per-day open-pit operation; the Western Zone depth extension suggests a larger system than originally modelled.

headline: RECORD SNOWFALL HITS CHILE: Anglo American Q3 copper output falls 5% — Collahuasi drops 11%, 2026 guidance held
snippet: Anglo American's Q3 2026 production report showed group copper output fell 5% year-on-year to 174,900 tonnes after record snowfall forced unplanned maintenance at Los Bronces and lower-grade stockpile ore was processed at Collahuasi, which dropped 11% to 42,000 attributable tonnes. Full-year 2026 copper guidance of 700,000–760,000 tonnes was maintained with ore grades expected to improve in Q4, but the weather-driven miss underlines how exposed Chile's open-pit copper mines remain to increasingly extreme precipitation events.

headline: AXO METALS DISCOVERS new Luz del Cobre gold target — 48m at 1.18 g/t Au from SURFACE in Sonora; high 3.94 g/t over 15m
snippet: Axo Metals Corp. (TSXV: AXO) intersected 48.0 metres grading 1.18 g/t gold — including 15.0 metres at 3.94 g/t gold — from surface in near-surface oxide material at the newly identified Luz del Cobre target within its San Antonio project in Sonora, Mexico. The discovery hole confirms a separate, oxidised gold system sitting above and adjacent to the Sapuchi copper-gold resource, adding a potentially low-cost heap-leach component to a project that was previously valued primarily for its sulphide copper.

headline: MAURITANIA'S FIRST URANIUM MINE: Aura Energy Tiris BFS returns US$500M NPV at 28% IRR — December FID target locked
snippet: Aura Energy's (ASX: AEE) bankable feasibility study for the Tiris uranium project in Mauritania returned a post-tax NPV of US$500.3 million at an 8% discount rate, a 28% IRR, and a 3.2-year payback — based on a flat US$90 per pound uranium price and capital cost of US$349.8 million. The company is targeting a final investment decision by December 2026 and first production in 2028 at 1.8 million pounds of U3O8 per year with AISC of US$41.25/lb, backed by a US utility offtake MOU and DFC senior debt discussions of up to US$170 million.

headline: BUENAVENTURA CUTS 2026 GOLD GUIDANCE to 142K–165K oz — silver suffers worst week of Q4 at -6.43%
snippet: Peru's Buenaventura revised its 2026 gold production guidance down to 142,300–164,500 ounces (from 163,300–186,500 oz) after tailings filtration constraints at the San Gabriel mine capped throughput, according to Frank Holmes' weekly Gold SWOT column on GoldSeek. Silver was the week's worst-performing precious metal at -6.43%, pushing the gold-silver ratio from 69.1 to 73.2 — a level analysts historically associate with silver being oversold relative to gold.

headline: RECORD RED INK: US fiscal 2026 deficit hits $1.99 TRILLION — third-largest in history, up 12% year-on-year
snippet: The US federal government recorded a fiscal year 2026 deficit of $1.99 trillion — the third-largest in history and 12% higher than FY2025's $1.78 trillion — per a Money Metals analysis by Mike Maharrey. For precious metals investors, the structural pattern matters: deficits of this scale require ongoing monetary financing that has historically coincided with sustained precious metals bull markets, and the trajectory shows no political path to correction before the mid-term election cycle.

headline: GOLD NEEDS $4,700 BACK: Kitco maps the conditions for $6,000 gold and silver's return above $90
snippet: Kitco analysts writing October 19 identify the key conditions for gold to reclaim $4,700 and ultimately test $6,000: a rebound in retail and institutional investor positioning (currently near multi-year lows after a 20% correction from January's $5,595 all-time high), a dovish FOMC signal on October 27–28, and a break in oil-driven real rate expectations. Silver's return above $90 is the lagging indicator analysts would watch to confirm a full renewal of the secular bull — the industrial-monetary demand combination is historically silver's signal to outperform.

headline: BARRICK AT $40 — Motley Fool bull case: gold major trades 6% below open while Q2 EPS surged 74%
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis (October 21) makes the bull case for Barrick Mining (NYSE: GOLD) at approximately $40 per share — down more than 6% year to date despite the company reporting Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.82, up 74% year on year, at an average realized gold price of $4,417 per ounce. The analysis argues Barrick's AISC well below current spot, a 25% dividend increase, and multi-decade reserve base make it a deeply undervalued gold equity relative to the secular gold price environment.
